meta.title: Threats, harassment, or blackmail: Cybercrime Report & Track
meta.description: This category is not built in this prototype. Here's what it is, why it isn't built, and what to actually do right now.

harassment.title: Threats, harassment, or blackmail
harassment.subtitle: Someone is threatening you, harassing you, or trying to blackmail you online, and you want to report it.
harassment.whatThisIsBody: This covers being threatened, stalked, or harassed through messages, calls, or social media, and blackmail or sextortion, where someone demands money or more content by threatening to share private images or information.
harassment.notBuiltBody: There is no reporting flow for this on this prototype. Only one journey is finished end to end: money taken from a bank account or UPI. This page is a real, honest stop, not a form in disguise.
harassment.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Call 1930
steps.body: India's national cybercrime helpline. It covers harassment, threats, and blackmail, not just financial fraud.

steps.title: Report on the real national portal
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in has a dedicated "Women/Children Related Crime" section, including an option to report anonymously without giving your name.

steps.title: Don't delete anything
steps.body: Keep the messages, screenshots, and profile or number involved exactly as they are. They may be needed as evidence.

steps.title: Don't pay, and don't engage further
steps.body: Paying blackmail rarely ends the demands. Screenshot everything and stop replying, then report it.

harassment.moneyNote: If money was also taken from you as part of this, our one finished journey covers that part.

hacked.title: Hacked account, or something else happened
hacked.subtitle: Your account, email, or online profile was taken over, or what happened to you doesn't fit anywhere else on this page.
hacked.whatThisIsBody: This covers a hacked email, social media, or other online account, someone impersonating you online, ransomware, and anything else that doesn't fit "money was taken from my account".
hacked.notBuiltBody: There is no reporting flow for this on this prototype. Only one journey is finished end to end: money taken from a bank account or UPI. This page is a real, honest stop, not a form in disguise.
hacked.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Secure the account first
steps.body: If you can still log in, change the password immediately and turn on two-factor authentication. If you can't log in, use the platform's own account-recovery flow.

steps.title: Call 1930
steps.body: India's national cybercrime helpline. It handles hacked accounts and impersonation, not just financial fraud.

steps.title: Report on the real national portal
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in has an "Other Cyber Crime" category that covers hacking, unauthorized access, and cases that don't fit elsewhere.

steps.title: Don't delete anything
steps.body: Keep screenshots, login-alert emails, and any message from the attacker exactly as they are. They may be needed as evidence.

hacked.moneyNote: If money was also taken from you as part of this, our one finished journey covers that part.

footerLinks: This page is honest about what it is: a real stop, not a workaround. See <whatsRealLink>what's real vs mocked</whatsRealLink> for the full picture, or <helpLink>what to do if money was just taken</helpLink> if that's part of what happened.
